root_cause.text: The bcmgenet TX timeout handler in `drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/genet/bcmgenet.c` incorrectly performed global recovery for all TX rings when only one `txqueue` timed out, creating races with still-active queues by reclaiming their descriptors, re-enabling their interrupts, and waking them unnecessarily.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `bcmgenet_timeout()` from looping over all `priv->tx_rings` with `bcmgenet_dump_tx_queue()`, calling `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all(dev)`, clearing interrupt masks for every queue, updating the whole device with `netif_trans_update(dev)`, and `netif_tx_wake_all_queues(dev)`, to operating only on `ring = &priv->tx_rings[txqueue]` and `txq = netdev_get_tx_queue(dev, txqueue)` via `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim(dev, ring, true)`, `bcmgenet_intrl2_1_writel(priv, 1 << txqueue, ...)`, `txq_trans_cond_update(txq)`, and `netif_tx_wake_queue(txq)`; the commit message explicitly says taking down all TX queues for a single timeout "causes many race conditions with queues that are still chugging along."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `bcmgenet_timeout()` from looping over all `priv->tx_rings` with `bcmgenet_dump_tx_queue()`, calling `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all(dev)`, clearing interrupt masks for every queue, updating the whole device with `netif_trans_update(dev)`, and `netif_tx_wake_all_queues(dev)`, to operating only on `ring = &priv->tx_rings[txqueue]` and `txq = netdev_get_tx_queue(dev, txqueue)` via `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim(dev, ring, true)`, `bcmgenet_intrl2_1_writel(priv, 1 << txqueue, ...)`, `txq_trans_cond_update(txq)`, and `netif_tx_wake_queue(txq)`; the commit message explicitly says taking down all TX queues for a single timeout "causes many race conditions with queues that are still chugging along."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TX timeout handling to recover only the timed-out BCMGENET transmit queue instead of affecting all queues.
intent_record.what: The timeout handler was changed from operating on all TX queues to operating only on the timed-out queue identified by txqueue: it now creates local ring and txq pointers, dumps only that ring, calls bcmgenet_tx_reclaim() for that ring instead of bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all(), removes the loop that built an interrupt mask for all queues, re-enables only the interrupt bit for txqueue, updates transmission timing with txq_trans_cond_update(txq) instead of netif_trans_update(dev), increments the error stat through ring->stats64, and wakes only the affected queue with netif_tx_wake_queue(txq) instead of netif_tx_wake_all_queues(dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, a TX timeout now triggers recovery only for the specific transmit queue that timed out rather than resetting or touching every TX queue. This limits reclaim, interrupt re-enable, timestamp update, debug dump, stats update, and queue wakeup to the affected ring, avoiding unnecessary interference with other queues and making multiqueue timeout handling more precise.

grouping_result.intent: Fix TX timeout handling to recover only the timed-out BCMGENET transmit queue instead of affecting all queues.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it narrows BCMGENET TX timeout recovery from all TX rings to only the timed-out queue, avoiding races and incorrect handling of active queues.

candidates.rationale: This globally reclaims descriptors for all TX rings during a timeout for a single txqueue, directly matching the root cause of racing with still-active queues.
This loop structure is part of the buggy all-queues recovery logic, causing operations to be applied to every TX ring instead of only the timed-out queue.
This accumulates interrupt re-enablement bits for every queue, re-enabling interrupts globally rather than only for the timed-out queue.
This wakes all transmit queues after a timeout on one queue, unnecessarily affecting still-active queues and contributing to the incorrect global recovery behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct cause of the bug: during timeout handling for a single timed-out txqueue, it reclaims descriptors for all TX rings, which can race with queues that are still active.
This loop drives the incorrect all-queues recovery behavior by iterating over every TX queue instead of limiting recovery actions to the specific timed-out queue.
Inside the all-queues timeout recovery path, this statement re-enables interrupts for every TX queue, including queues that did not time out, contributing to races with still-active queues.
This wakes all transmit queues after recovery from a timeout affecting only one txqueue, unnecessarily perturbing other active queues and forming part of the incorrect global recovery logic.
